title: Did I just find a stalker's USB?
captions: I found a USB labeled ‘Do Not Plug In’ on my new desk. #storytime #fyp #foryou #drama #mystery #tech
The USB might be a trap, but I need answers. #storytime #fyp #foryou #drama #suspense #tech
I see myself being watched. What would you do? #storytime #fyp #foryou #drama #mystery #verdict
parts: [[DAY 1 · 09:12]] I found a USB labeled ‘Do Not Plug In’ on the back of my new desk. [[RULE 1 · CURIOUS]] My hands shake as I lift it. The plastic feels cold, like a breath on skin. I stare at the empty office, the hum of the air‑conditioner filling the silence. [[9:45 AM · KITCHEN]] I make coffee, the kettle whistling, and the USB sits on the counter, humming in my mind. [[THIRTY MINUTES LEFT]] My roommate texts, “Did you get the charger?” I pretend it’s nothing. [[RULE 2 · IGNORE]] I pull out my laptop, stare at the blank desktop. The cursor blinks, daring me. I hear a faint click behind the door—just the building’s old pipes. I take a breath, decide to plug it in. The screen flashes. A folder opens. Inside, a single video file named “WATCH”. My heart pounds. I double‑click. The video loads. Nothing plays at first. Then a grainy view flickers on screen. [[3 MINUTES LEFT]] I recognize my own bedroom door, the cracked mirror, the chipped coffee mug on the nightstand. The camera angle is exactly where my phone usually sits on the dresser. My pulse spikes. I glance at the phone—still charging, screen dark. I hear a soft thump above my head. I freeze. [[5 MINUTES LEFT]] The video shows a figure stepping into the frame, right behind me. I turn, but the room is empty. The figure is still on screen, breathing. I stare, terrified, as the clock on the wall ticks down. Then—

My breath catches. [[DAY 1 · 10:05]] The video is still playing, the figure inches closer to the camera. I can hear my own breathing echoing in the room. The sound of my phone vibrating on the desk snaps me back. A text flashes: “You’re still watching?” I stare at the screen, heart hammering. [[RULE 3 · DECIDE]] I reach for the USB, fingers trembling, ready to yank it out. The figure on the video lifts a hand—my own hand, but turned inside‑out, the camera lens exposed. My mind reels. I realize the phone on the desk is the source. [[10 MINUTES LEFT]] I yank the USB, the video freezes on a frame of my own eye, wide with shock. The room feels colder, the air heavier. I hear a faint click from the hallway, as if someone just locked the door. I glance at the window; rain patters against the glass, each drop a tiny drumbeat. My phone buzzes again, this time a call from an unknown number. I stare at the screen, the caller ID reads “UNKNOWN”. I consider answering, but the thought of hearing a voice behind the camera makes my skin crawl. [[RULE 4 · HIDE]] I slip the USB into my pocket, decide to hide the phone in the bathroom cabinet. The ticking clock on the wall now feels like a countdown. I hear footsteps outside the door, slow, deliberate. I hold my breath, waiting. The handle turns. The door cracks open just enough to let a sliver of light in. I brace for the worst.

My lease ends in 24 minutes, and the USB could seal my fate.

The door bursts open. [[DAY 1 · 10:12]] A silhouette slides in, toolbox clanking, eyes flicking over everything. He stops at my desk, spots the USB glinting on the floor, and grins. “Found it,” he whispers, low and hungry. My stomach flips.

He snatches the USB, turns it over, then pulls a tiny camera—my phone, smashed, lens jutting out. “You’ve been watching yourself,” he chuckles, the sound echoing off the walls. My breath catches.

It’s my brother, the one I haven’t spoken to in years. He says he rigged the camera to check on me after I moved out, but the phone slipped, the lens broke, and the footage leaked. “I’ll delete it and go,” he says, hands trembling.

A buzz shatters the silence. A text from an unknown number: “You’re free now.” I glance at the digital clock—23:58. The lease timer ticks down. I have seconds.

Do I trust him and keep the proof, or erase everything and disappear before the lease flips? I stare at the broken phone, the USB, the blinking cursor of the countdown. The room feels colder, the air thick with static.

I lock eyes with the camera for the last time. So… was I wrong to keep watching, or should I wipe it all and run?

premise.hook: I found a USB labeled ‘Do Not Plug In’ on the back of my new desk.
premise.twist: Plugging it in reveals a live feed of the narrator’s apartment—someone has been watching them for weeks, and the camera is actually their own phone turned inside‑out.
premise.debate: Comments will split on whether the narrator should confront the stalker or erase all evidence and run.
